result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both recommend B, explain that a multiple-choice test checks recognition rather than live production, and calculate the 15 hours correctly. B turns the constraint into a concrete plan: peer pairs for the first two rounds and the team lead only for the third, which brings the lead's time to about 5 hours spread over a few days. It also adds a scenario quiz and a plan to measure results against a baseline the team already tracks. A's ideas (triads, recordings, a facts check and a fallback) are solid, but its 60–70% reduction is a loose estimate rather than a worked-out schedule. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers recommend B and make the same core point: a multiple-choice test shows whether a rep can recognize a good answer, not whether they can give one out loud. Both work out the roughly 15 hours of team-lead time. Answer A is more precise about cutting that to about 5 hours, and it adds a useful check on whether the gap is knowledge or delivery. Answer B offers more concrete ways to keep scale (peer triads, recorded sessions reviewed later, a facts-only auto-scored check) plus a fallback if the lead has no time; its facts-only quiz also fits its own argument better than A's 'what do you say next' scenario quiz.
